LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.8: Imitative Speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Imitative Speaking. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can one communicate clearly and effectively?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify words, phrases and expressions in varied texts

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Imitative Speaking helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Work jointly to repeat sentences on weather features using the sentence structure “这 是...... ”(e.g. 这是太阳; 太阳很大;这 是云 ),
2. Communication and Collaboration: Teamwork skills are fostered as the learner works together with their peers to ask and respond to questions related to weather features.
3. Digital literacy: The learner connects and uses the internet to research on extreme weather events with peers. Values:
4. Respect: The learner appreciates the diverse opinions given as they evaluate their peer’s pronunciation.
5. Listen and write down vocabulary of the different items found at home, ( 花园、沙 发 、浴室、窗户、门 ),

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can one communicate clearly and effectively?
2. How do you get information from oral texts?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
